I farm cotton on all 13.1 mu, so I will keep the whole farm in cotton this year. I have been doing this a long time, and at the start of the season I care most about keeping the crop stable, controlling costs, and making sure the field work fits my household labor since some people work off-farm. Because I have well irrigation, I will not depend only on rainfall, so I will push for a steady stand and protect yield with a moderate but reliable input plan. I will use improved seed rather than traditional seed because I want better emergence, more even growth, and more dependable production. I will prepare the land with rotary tillage because it is practical for my scale and lets me get the seedbed ready quickly. For fertilizer, I will stay in a moderate range: enough nitrogen to support vegetative growth and boll setting, with phosphorus and potassium to support roots, early growth, and yield stability. I will irrigate several times through the season because cotton here can suffer if early growth, flowering, or boll filling runs short of water. I will also spray pesticides several times because cotton usually needs steady insect control if I want to avoid yield loss. With this kind of management, I will aim for a solid, realistic yield rather than taking big risks.
